chunk_map.heading: Phase 1: Read what the failed run did
Make Claude show its work, make it dig
Phase 2: Match each failure to the check that catches it
Phase 3: Build the verifier for your worst failure
Phase 4: Write the reference and plan.md
Check both files are for the agent, not you
Send it off and read the report cold

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a reader loses the thread when a pronoun/noun has no antecedent they can hold. Walked all 13 chunks in expanded-view line order (expand-md.js run this session), fences excluded. 'three failure-mode lenses' (chunk 1 line 40) resolves to chunk 0 line 15's own naming one chunk prior. Chunk 3 line 71's 'Drift and context rot ... Plausible-but-wrong' names are never defined inside this file's own body before this point, but verified via `grep -n 'goal drift' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/learn-from-the-test.md` this session -> line 15's 'What You'll Learn' bullet names 'three named lenses, goal drift, context rot, plausible-but-wrong' before this exercise's include-link (line 46 of that file), so §1's module-include-order carve-out applies: arc-earned vocabulary from the enclosing module's signposting. Chunk 6's 'Reference'/'plan.md' handles were already named informally at chunk 0 line 17 ('a verifier, a reference, and a plan.md') and are formally defined at first full use — not a violation, a definition. No unresolved referent found; harm absent.

Harm: a callback that depends on which file/module sits where breaks under re-sequencing. Three candidates, all name the source rather than locate it. Chunk 2 line 64: 'Same prior as the repo read in Module 1: assume about 10% of the account misrepresents the run' names the source by module number and unpacks the claim (the 10% prior) in the same sentence. Chunk 10 line 200: 'the field has a name for this move ... see [What packaging is](lectures/what-packaging-is.md)' names the document in the link text; the sentence still reads with the link stripped. Chunk 11 (module-flag branch) line 234: 'the walk-away report at the close is what Module 6 opens on' names the target module by number, not by position ('the next module'). Same chunk, line 236: 'Same cancel-is-legit rule as the un-packaged session' names the rule by its claim ('cancel-is-legit') and anchors it to the student's own M4 session rather than locating it by file position. No position-dependent phrasing ('above', 'the opening lecture', 'earlier module') found anywhere in body. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: 'the X you did/saw' pointing at a beat the module's current file set doesn't have strands the reader. Two candidates. (a) Chunk 11 line 234 (module-flag branch): 'The walk-away report at the close is what Module 6 opens on.' Ran `grep -n slug: site/layouts/curriculum.js` this session: 'learn-from-the-test' (confirmed as this file's host module via `grep -n diagnose-and-resend curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/learn-from-the-test.md` -> line 46 include-link) sits immediately before 'spot-gaps-build-the-loop' in MODULES order — M6 exists and is the true next module. (b) Chunk 11 line 236: 'Same cancel-is-legit rule as the un-packaged session.' Ran `grep -rn cancel curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/*.md curriculum/exercises/*.md curriculum/lectures/*.md` this session: the beat lives at exercises/set-the-markers-send-it-off.md:77 ('trainer names cancel-is-legit — stop it when you've seen enough. Traces are data.') and as the named claim `cancel-is-legitimate` in lectures/test-and-learn.md's backing block; both files are confirmed M4 content via run-the-first-experiment.md's own include links (lines 37, 43). Both backward references resolve to real beats. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a guess-before-reveal instruction whose answer is narrated above it spoils the beat on a text read. Scanned all 13 chunks: the file's shape is diagnose -> match -> build -> prove -> assemble -> resend; no guess/predict-then-reveal construction exists anywhere in body. Rule doesn't apply.

Harm: a chunk whose only content is a wait-state or one context-dependent bullet projects as a slide that says nothing standalone. Shortest chunks checked: chunk 9 'Approve' (182-185, 'Say lock it in. The agent writes both files.') names the trigger phrase and its effect — self-carrying. Chunk 2 (61-65) carries two substantive push-back bullets. Chunk 6 (135-141) defines both artefacts in four bullets. Every chunk carries multiple substantive sentences or a fenced prompt. Harm absent.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts misleads a reader who only skims headers. Checked all 12 `##` headers against their chunk bodies: 'Make Claude show its work, make it dig' -> push-back-for-quotes-and-verification content (line 63-64); 'Check both files are for the agent, not you' -> glance-and-push-back-on-genericness content (179-180); 'Send it off and read the report cold' -> re-send prompt + candour-check content (212-236). Every header is a true summary of its own chunk. Harm absent.

Harm: repo-authored prose tics read as filler once wall-projected. Ran `grep -niE 'not [a-z]+\.[[:space:]]*not [a-z]+\.'` over body (lines 1-243, fences included in scan but no hits found in prose either): 0 hits (Not-X-Not-Y ban). Ran `grep -niE 'one of the most|most useful|best way'` over body: 0 hits (self-grading superlative). Manually re-read every chunk for anaphora/epistrophe triples, verb triplets with an empty leg, and abstraction-noun stacks: none found. The one number instance in body ('about 10%', chunk 2 line 64) has no retraction phrase in this file; maintainer block (line 248, outside evaluated scope but confirms intent) states 'M1's double-hedge ... stays M1's, so §7's number-plus-retraction sub-item does not fire here.' Harm absent on every sub-item.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: repo/maintainer vocabulary smuggled onto a slide reads as unparseable jargon to an engineer in the room. Ran `grep -niE '\bsurface\b|\beval\b|compendium|forcing function|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b| firing |Connections\b'` over body (lines 1-243): 0 hits. 'judges it' (chunk 4 line 100, background-agent verifier definition) is the ordinary LLM-as-judge engineering pattern, not this repo's class-judge system — audience-appropriate for AE101 engineer ICs. 'stop-hook' (chunk 4 line 101) is Claude Code product terminology. 'Ralph re-feed'/'Ralph's fresh-sessions camp'/'Amp's manual-handoff camp' (chunks 4, 10) name real practitioner techniques per the backing block, not house dialect. 'RLHF' (chunk 11 line 234) is a standard, widely-known ML term, not repo-internal. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: bold-monoculture (whole sentences/leads bolded) buries the actual handles and reads as noise once wall-projected. Located every `**...**` span by hand across the 13 chunks: chunk 0 has 6 (Time/Session/HOX/What-you-do/-build/-point) — title-page widget chrome, exempt per the file's own maintainer Emphasis note. Chunk 4 has 3, one per verifier-shape bullet (Background-agent verifier / Deterministic shell-hook / Ralph re-feed) — matches the reading-list/menu-slide carve-out, each a short handle. Chunk 6 has 2 (Reference / plan.md) — one handle per defined term. Chunk 10 has 1 (Session widget) — chrome. Chunk 7 has 1: the full sentence 'Cut the grill when the package is good enough to re-send.' — the only full-sentence bold in the file. Weighed against harm: no monoculture pattern exists elsewhere in the file (every other span is a 1-3 word handle or chrome), the maintainer block names it as a deliberate stop-gate signal, and it functions as the load-bearing handle for the Phase-4 lock-in gate — the harm (noise/monoculture) this rule exists to prevent is not present here. Flagging it would ask the maintainer to shorten the file's one deliberate stop-gate signal, degrading the artefact. Rule question noted, not filed as REVISE.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: content invisible to the layout a reader is actually in reads as silently missing. This file is reached via a standalone-paragraph include link (`[Exercise: Diagnose and re-send](exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md)`, confirmed at learn-from-the-test.md:46); the renderer wraps included exercise files under `.phase--exercise`, which reaches `buildDeckModel`. This file carries no prework/supplementary/reference-shaped section (the surface types the 2026-07-09 incident dropped) — all content sits inside Phase/`##` headings under the exercise proper, including the flag-conditional chunk 12, which `applyContentFlags` resolves before the deck is built. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: hand-numbered or inconsistent Phase/Step ordinals strand in-file cross-references. Ran `node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md` this session: output 'OK — 61 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.' Phase headers run 1-5 consecutively; in-file forward refs ('Phase 3 builds the verifier against the dominant failure; Phase 4 assembles...' chunk 3 line 92, 'Fire it once before Phase 4' chunk 5 line 127) resolve to real later headers. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a positional pointer ('below'/'above'/'at the top of this page') aims at a wall once the renderer cuts at `##`. Ran `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md` this session: output 'OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' The one below/above-shaped phrase in body, chunk 11 line 212 'the re-send prompt below stands alone,' points at the fenced prompt on lines 218-232 — the SAME chunk, matching the compendium's own canonical same-chunk-passes shape. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a dead in-deck link, or one that is unnamed/geometry-located (both settled corpus-wide, mechanism fixed 2026-08-12). Ran `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --links --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md` this session: one link found, chunk 10 line 200 'What packaging is' -> lectures/what-packaging-is.md, named in the link text, not located by page position. Harm absent; explicitly a review surface, never a gate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: an over-cap chunk gets trimmed off-schedule or, if missed, over-projects on the wall unnoticed. Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md` this session: 'files: 1  slides: 11  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets ... oversized: 0 ... ✓ every slide is within limits.' No `**Slide size accepted:**` note needed. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: an exercise heading phrased as a lecture-style claim blurs the imperative-vs-declarative mood signal the deck relies on. Read all 12 `##` headers: ten are imperative or 'Phase N:' phase labels (e.g. 'Read what the failed run did', 'Make Claude show its work, make it dig', 'Build the verifier for your worst failure', 'Prove the verifier actually fires', 'Check both files are for the agent, not you', 'Approve', 'Send it off and read the report cold', 'Bring the worktree's work home'). Two are bare topic-noun labels, not truth-claims: 'The reference and plan.md' and its echo 'Phase 4: Write the reference and plan.md' — neither asserts a claim the way this training's two calibrated exercise declaratives do (close-the-ticket.md's 'Anything can be reverse-engineered', fix-tests-first.md's 'There is always a next plausible answer'). No declarative-claim heading found in this file. Harm absent.
